identity.title: Advancing Expert Specialization for Better MoE

problem.claim: The paper addresses expert routing in Mixture-of-Experts models, where only a subset of experts is activated per input.

gap.claim: The authors report that commonly used auxiliary load-balancing loss can cause expert overlap and overly uniform routing, limiting specialization and degrading post-training performance.

contributions.claim: A training approach adds orthogonality and variance objectives to encourage distinct expert token processing and more discriminative routing.
A gradient-level analysis reports that the two objectives are compatible with the existing auxiliary loss and support training optimization.
The authors report improved expert specialization across model architectures and multiple benchmarks, without architectural modifications or additional components.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors distinguish their approach by jointly using complementary orthogonality and variance losses to improve specialization while retaining the existing load-balancing setup.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that the objectives improve classic MoE baselines using auxiliary loss by up to 23.79%.
The authors report enhanced specialization across various architectures and multiple benchmarks.
The authors report that downstream tasks maintain load balancing while using the proposed method.

narrative_sequence.summary: MoE models scale LLMs efficiently by activating only subsets of experts per input.
The authors identify overlap and overly uniform routing under common auxiliary load balancing, with negative post-training effects.
They introduce orthogonality and variance losses, then report gradient-level compatibility with the auxiliary objective.
They report specialization gains across architectures and benchmarks, including up to 23.79% improvement, and state that code will be released.

source_observation.claim: The abstract links a concrete routing pathology to two complementary objectives targeting distinct expert processing and discriminative decisions.

lessons.interpretation: A method can be motivated more convincingly when each added objective is explicitly tied to a diagnosed failure mode.
lessons.application: For a new training method, map each auxiliary objective to a specific observed behavior and state the intended direction of change.
lessons.exception: This framing is unsuitable when the objectives lack an identifiable mechanism or the observed pathology is not measured.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the architectures, benchmarks, downstream tasks, or experimental conditions.
The scope and baseline details behind the maximum 23.79% improvement are unspecified.
The abstract does not provide quantitative specialization or load-balancing metrics.
Code release is stated as future work; availability and reproducibility are not established.
